scope: Independent read-only review of the isolated three-arm development pilot; no GPU, submission, model load, or frozen-source edit.
corrected_during_review: The score finisher now parses and validates completion records, binds image sidecars to those records and protocol/source pins, checks config digests and PNG hashes, and rejects failed or incomplete generation.
ImageReward cached checkpoint and configuration paths and SHA256 values are checked before generation and again during score acceptance. Other scorer model revisions match the archived reference.

Worker acceptance now verifies the exact 57 block names, per-block counts, per-step geometry checks, declared mode/grid/backend/text policy, native identity flag, numerical policy and expected old-text/new-text/image-only branch counts.
Saved initial and final tensor receipts are checked against the actual finite BF16 tensors and their byte hashes, not only file hashes.
Worker fixed-mass range validation now uses the processor FP32 exp(log_mass_upper_tolerance) ceiling rather than an inconsistent strict-one ceiling. No clipping was added.

Design and feasibility documents now declare the stable separate image-only unnormalized control, its approximately99.225percent extra attention arithmetic, fixed-mass approximately1.538percent extra arithmetic, query_chunk_size65536 and cosine diagnostic policy.
verified_by_source_inspection: The alternate image query is formed from the actual normalized pre-RoPE query, with base rotary frequencies and endpoint coordinates p*63/(L-1); original BF16 rotary-pair gains are retained.
Only the image-query/text-key branch is replaced. All 512 text keys, including padding, are included. Zero text IDs and raster image IDs are checked explicitly.
The fixed-mass formula is joint_output + old_text_mass*(new_text_conditional_output-old_text_conditional_output), evaluated in FP32 before BF16 conversion.

The unnormalized control uses separate image-only and new-text conditional attention with a stable logaddexp mixture. It does not recover image contributions by subtracting rounded text output from the full baseline.

Native 64x64 grid arms use the same full joint backend path, bypassing correction. Full-model native smoke requires byte-identical phase-arm endpoints and measures deployed-public versus private-backend endpoint error.

The worker records actual initial packed input hashes and requires identical initial input and conditioning hashes across arms. It records gains, sigmas, final latent hashes, configuration and source provenance.
Per-arm teardown restores processors and the prior runtime hooks. New scorer roots are task-local images directories, with exactly three arms and two existing development prompt indices.
The fleet uses a two-node spool and exact recorded telemetry process-group cleanup. No broad process kill or scratch deletion appeared in reviewed scripts.
limits: No GPU behavior, full image-attention production geometry, image quality, or runtime has been verified by this review. The prospective smoke includes a24-head/65536-query/512-key text branch with production projection strides. The full65536-image-key branch is still first exercised during generation; its support is not established by the text-only probe.
The unnormalized control adds roughly another image attention pass and is not an equal-cost method arm. Sequential arm timings are not a warmup-matched performance benchmark.

Fixed-mass conservation is exact algebraically, but separate BF16 conditional outputs and FP32 LSE introduce finite-precision residuals. The implementation checks finite values and bounded log mass; it does not establish bitwise conservation at 4K.

The native deployed-versus-private relative-L2 tolerance is an engineering parity criterion, not a rigorous BF16 roundoff theorem. The current worker makes cosine diagnostic and must keep that distinction in the frozen protocol.
The phase hypothesis is provisional. Prior-art ingredients are known; this review establishes neither novelty nor efficacy, and CR20 did not reveal a primary native-success/4K-failure pair.
